core_obligations: Prove the etale case: an etale ring map is flat and the map B tensor_A B -> B is again etale as a map between etale A-algebras (proof lines 30465-30468).
For a directed system B_i of weakly etale A-algebras, conclude that the colimit B is flat over A by the colimit-of-flat-maps statement (proof lines 30471-30473).

Note that the transition maps B_i -> B_{i'} are flat by permanence of weak etaleness, hence that B is flat over B_i for each i, and conclude that B is flat over B_i tensor_A B_i by composition of flat maps (proof lines 30474-30478).
Conclude that B is flat over B tensor_A B = colim (B_i tensor_A B_i) by the colimit-of-rings-flat statement, which proves the colimit case (proof lines 30479-30480).
Obtain the localization case directly or as a combination of the previous two (proof lines 30483-30484).
difficulty_reason: The lemma lists three cases in which a ring map A -> B is weakly etale: when B is a localization of A; when A -> B is etale; and when B is a filtered colimit of weakly etale A-algebras (source lines 30453-30462). The proof treats the etale case first: an etale ring map is flat and the multiplication B tensor_A B -> B is again etale as a map between etale A-algebras, which is exactly the conjunction defining weak etaleness (proof lines 30465-30468). The colimit case is the substantive part: for a directed system B_i of weakly etale A-algebras, the colimit B is flat over A by the colimit-of-flat-maps statement; the transition maps B_i -> B_{i'} are flat by permanence of weak etaleness, so B is flat over each B_i and hence flat over B_i tensor_A B_i by composition of flat maps; and therefore B is flat over B tensor_A B = colim (B_i tensor_A B_i) by the colimit-of-rings-flat statement (proof lines 30471-30480). The localization case is then obtained directly or as a combination of the other two (proof lines 30483-30484). The non-routine content is the systematic use of flatness permanence to transport flatness of the multiplication maps along the colimit.
